newsitem.title: USA: Donna Karan up after 'restricted' report.
newsitem.headline: Donna Karan up after 'restricted' report.

text.p: Shares of Donna Karan International Inc jumped 19 percent Wednesday after a fund manager made bullish comments on television and said the company was on the restricted list at Morgan Stanley.
Shares closed up 1-7/8 to 11-3/4, making the stock the top gainer on the New York Stock Exchange on a percent basis.
Analysts said Polo Ralph Lauren's proposed initial public offering has also refocused the spotlight on premium clothing designers and manufacturers.
Speaking on CNBC, Robert Olsten of the Olstein Financial Alert Fund said he recommended buying shares of the designer and said the stock was on Morgan Stanley's restricted list.
Morgan Stanley could not be reached for comment.

Being on a "restricted list" means the broker cannot trade the stock for its own accounts and its analysts cannot comment on a stock because either an analyst has inside information on the company, or the company and the brokerage are involved in corporate finance relationship.
The relationship could be something small, such as a licensing deal, but it could also mean something as significant as a merger or stock offering.
"The stock has been hurt. It's near its low of nine and with Ralph Lauren going public, it's encouraging for high-end branded manufacturers," said Peter Schaeffer of Dillon Read.
Olstein said on CNBC the company will sell its beauty license "imminently", will triple its margins, will generate 'huge' cash flow going forward and is worth over $20 a share.
Donna Karan shares went public last year at $24 each, but have steadily declined since.
Olstein added he like Loehmann's Inc. Its shares fell 21 percent in heavy trading losing 2-7/8 to 10-3/8, making it one of the top losing stocks on the Nasdaq on a percent basis.
